messages:
maya: Heads-up — hit a nasty combo of token refresh race + 429s while running the onboarding sample-app. Repro steps and logs below.

leo: Ugh. Can you paste the minimal repro (curl or snippet) + the exact 429 headers you saw?

maya: Steps: 1) Start sample-app with --short-token-lifetime=5s 2) Hammer /v1/generate with 10 concurrent clients 3) Token refresh kicks in, multiple inflight requests replay with no idempotency key and backend rate-limits to 429.

Logs (truncated):
```
[2026-01-12T12:03:01Z] request id=abc123 status=401 msg="token expired"
[2026-01-12T12:03:01Z] refresh start for user=u42
[2026-01-12T12:03:01Z] request id=def456 status=429 Retry-After: 2
[2026-01-12T12:03:02Z] request id=ghi789 status=429
[2026-01-12T12:03:04Z] refresh done token=tok_XXXXX
[2026-01-12T12:03:05Z] request id=jkl012 status=200 latency=45ms
```

maya: Important bits: 429s had Retry-After sometimes, sometimes not. No Idempotency-Key on requests. JS SDK auto-retried 429 but Python raised immediate error in my test.

sophie: That sounds like two separate problems: (1) token refresh single-flight, (2) idempotency keys / safe-replay, (3) consistent 429 handling across SDKs.

sam: Agreed. For 429 we should: honor `Retry-After` header if present, otherwise use exponential backoff with full jitter. Example (recommended):
```
base = 100ms
sleep = random_between(0, base * 2 ** attempt)
```
This prevents thundering herd.

sophie: Also parity note: JS SDK currently treats 429 as retryable by default, Python does not. We should standardize: retryable for 429 except when the endpoint is non-idempotent and no Idempotency-Key provided. Add config knobs: `retryOn429` and `treat429AsThrottling`.

leo: For token refresh races we added a single-flight promise in the runtime last quarter. i.e., first request triggers refresh, subsequent inflight requests wait on the refresh promise instead of refreshing themselves. SDKs need to do the same. Pseudocode: 
```
let refreshInFlight = null
async function getAccessToken() {
  if (token.valid) return token
  if (!refreshInFlight) refreshInFlight = doRefresh()
  await refreshInFlight
  refreshInFlight = null
  return token
}
```

maya: That + attaching `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` for client-initiated operations solved the sample-app locally. Backend then deduped repeated requests.

sam: Edge case: if the idempotency keys are only stored for a short TTL, long retries might still replay. We should recommend server TTL >= maxRetryWindow (e.g., 5 minutes).

sophie: Also note safe defaults: SDK should auto-add Idempotency-Key for POSTs where the route is in our catalog of safe-replay endpoints, and allow opt-out. Document this clearly in onboarding.

leo: Can you open a tiny patch to the sample-app with a reproduction script and a README? @deploy-bot can we get the sample-app CI to run the repro on PRs? :robot_face:

maya: Pushed branch: github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/compare/refresh-429-fix (contains: repro script, README, and a small SDK wrapper patch). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/pull/42

deploy-bot: CI scheduled for PR #42 — will run the repro job on linux/x86 and report flaky counts.

sam: Follow-ups we should track: 1) SDK parity ticket (JS/Python/Rust) for 429 behavior 2) Add single-flight token-refresh helper exported by all official SDKs 3) Doc page: "Retry semantics and idempotency best practices" 4) Backend: extend idempotency TTL to 5m by default.

maya: I'll file the tickets and link them to the PR. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
